title: Locked automation toolchain
$comment: The technology decision after a deterministic resolver has checked it. The architect proposes an ecosystem, a runtime, a test framework and the packages it needs; this file is what actually exists, pinned to exact versions from a real feed. Everything downstream - manifests, lock files, verification, the pipelines that run the suites - is generated from this and never from the proposal, so a run cannot build against a version nobody confirmed.

blueprintSha256.$comment: The blueprint this was resolved from. A later stage can tell whether the design it is reading is the design this lock belongs to.

runtime.$comment: The runtime the toolchain was resolved against, under the names its adapter's ReadRuntime produces - nodeMajor, sdkMajor, pythonVersion - and never under the configuration's snake_case spelling. The translation happens once, where this file is written; a reader that translates a second time looks up node_major in a document that holds nodeMajor, finds nothing, and reports that it verified a framework against version zero.

version.$comment: Exact. A range here would be a decision deferred to whoever runs the resolver next.

requested.$comment: What the architect asked for. Kept so a reviewer can see the distance between the proposal and what the feed actually had.

decidedFor.$comment: The automation projects that made this decision. Projects that decided identically share one locked toolchain, which is what lets one manifest serve several of them.
